questions.q: Name two materials that are good electrical conductors and two materials that are good electrical insulators.
questions.a: Copper and iron are conductors; rubber and plastic are insulators. A wrong answer here shows the student has not yet distinguished between metals and non-metals in the context of electrical flow.

questions.q: If you were building a simple circuit with a battery and a bulb, why would you choose a copper wire instead of a cotton thread to connect them?
questions.a: Copper is a conductor and allows the current to flow, while cotton thread is an insulator and will stop the current. A wrong answer suggests the student does not understand that materials have different properties regarding electrical flow.

questions.q: You have a metal spoon and a wooden spoon. If you touch an electric wire with the metal spoon, it is dangerous. Why is it safe to touch the wooden handle of a toaster?
questions.a: The metal spoon conducts electricity from the wire to you, causing a shock, while the wood acts as an insulator, blocking the current from reaching your hand. This requires identifying the material property (conductor vs. insulator) and applying it to a safety situation.

questions.q: Analyze a standard electrical plug. It has metal pins and a plastic body. Explain why both materials are necessary for it to function safely.
questions.a: The metal pins are required to conduct electricity into the device, while the plastic body is required to insulate the user from touching the live current. A failure here indicates an inability to analyze how components serve different functional roles.

questions.q: Critique this statement: "All solid materials are conductors." Is this true or false, and why?
questions.a: This is false; while metals are conductors, many solids like wood, glass, and plastic are insulators. A wrong answer shows the student is over-generalizing based on the state of matter rather than the material's internal property.

questions.q: Imagine you are stranded and need to fix a broken wire in a toy. You have a piece of dry wood, a steel nail, and a thick piece of rubber. Which would you use to bridge the gap in the wire, and why?
questions.a: You would use the steel nail because it is a metal conductor. A poor answer would suggest using rubber or wood, showing a lack of understanding of which material facilitates current flow.
